quizName: Hardest Questions in Wyoming Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It has a white background with red and black markings. It tells drivers what traffic laws apply in this area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A red, octagonal sign is always a stop sign. When you see this sign, you must come to a complete stop. Let any other traffic or pedestrians pass. Then proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: Use your mirrors when stopping at an intersection:

options.text: To determine if drivers behind you are aware that you are stopping.
To look for dark clouds that may indicate poor weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: To determine if drivers behind you are aware that you are stopping.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to see vehicles coming up behind you. This helps you know if drivers see you and your actions. When stopping at an intersection, use your mirrors to make sure drivers behind you are reacting to your stop.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed. Avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes gently when you need to slow down.

questions.question: Whichever style of helmet you choose, you will get the most protection by ensuring that your helmet:
questions.explanation: Your helmet will protect you best if it fits snugly all the way around. It should meet U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should have no cracks or other damage.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, you should ensure that it:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around. Check that it has no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: You have an improved chance of surviving a crash if you wear:
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards gives you the best head and neck protection. Wearing a good-quality helmet that is properly fastened is the single best thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: A passenger should sit:
questions.explanation: Passengers must always sit behind the operator. They should hold firmly onto the operator's waist, hips, or midsection. They can also hold onto handgrips if the motorcycle has them. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, you should be most concerned about the helmet's:
questions.explanation: Protection should be your top priority when buying a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: The best clothing for a motorcyclist:

options.text: Should not stand out to other motorists.

questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you if you crash. They should also keep you comfortable and make sure other drivers can see you.

questions.question: Choose a lane position that makes you visible and gives you space around your motorcycle.

options.text: Makes you visible and gives you safe space around your motorcycle.
You prefer, regardless of other riders.
Puts you close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you visible and gives you safe space around your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Position yourself where other drivers can see you best. Keep space around your motorcycle for safety. The best lane position changes based on road conditions. Good riders adjust their position as needed.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Start slowing down earlier than usual.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. Extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to speed up, slow down, and turn. With a passenger, reduce your speed and start slowing earlier. Also look for larger gaps when entering or merging into traffic.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same place as on your motorcycle.
Take it on the highway right away.
Learn to use it in a safe, controlled area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn to use it in a safe, controlled area first.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding a new motorcycle, find all the controls. Practice riding it in a safe, controlled area before taking it on the road.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to make yourself visible to other drivers, even during the day. Reflective clothing is also helpful.

questions.question: What is most important when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important thing when buying a helmet. Choose a helmet that fits well, fastens securely, and is DOT-approved.

questions.question: When nearing a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will yield correctly.
Change your lane position to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position to be more visible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the lane position where other drivers can see you best.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Check that your brake lights work properly.
Check that the paint is not peeling.
Make sure your motorcycle is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that your brake lights work properly.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle's safety features before every ride. Test each brake to make sure the brake lights turn on.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: All keep safe distance from each other.
Follow each other as closely as possible.
Not worry about distances between riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: All keep safe distance from each other.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, use a staggered formation. This lets riders stay together while keeping safe distance between each other.

questions.question: Improper braking:

options.text: Is not a concern because motorcycles have two brakes.

questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Using correct braking technique is essential for safe riding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns of a railroad crossing.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce fatigue while driving?
questions.explanation: Taking frequent rest breaks during long trips helps reduce fatigue. Caffeine and other stimulants can make fatigue worse when they wear off. Bad weather can also increase fatigue, so dress warmly and protect yourself from wind and rain.

questions.question: When driving at night, how easy is it to judge distances?

options.text: About the same as during the day.
More difficult than during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than during the day.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances at night than during the day. Shadows and light help you see how far away things are. At night, artificial lights can distort or hide these important clues.

questions.question: What do reflective and brightly-colored helmets and clothing do?

options.text: Should only be worn when riding at night.
Help motorcycle riders be more visible.
Do not increase a motorcycle rider's safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help motorcycle riders be more visible.
questions.explanation: Wearing bright or reflective clothing makes other drivers more likely to see you on the road.

questions.question: What should you know about taking over-the-counter medication before riding?

options.text: It is usually fine since over-the-counter medications are not very strong.
It may affect your riding and should be done carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may affect your riding and should be done carefully.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, can impair your ability to safely ride. Always talk to your doctor about how a new medication may affect your riding.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol quickly?

options.text: The alcohol leaves your body faster.
The alcohol builds up in your body faster.
The alcohol affects your body less.

questions.correctAnswerText: The alcohol builds up in your body faster.
questions.explanation: Drinking quickly causes alcohol to build up in your body. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your system after an hour passes.
